options_firewall_howItWorks.message:
Blocked sites always win: a blocked entry beats any allowed entry.
If the allowed list is empty, every site that isn't blocked is reachable.
If the allowed list has entries, the agent can only open sites that match one.
example.com also covers every subdomain (www.example.com, a.b.example.com); *.example.com means the same.
github.com/org covers that path and everything below it, but not github.com/organic.
Add a port (localhost:3000) to match only that port.
A site sits on one list at a time; adding it to one list takes it off the other.
chrome://, file:, data: and the Chrome Web Store are always blocked.

options_memory_secretRejected.message: That looks like a password or key, so it was not stored. Keep it in the browser's password manager instead.

options_memory_howItWorks.message:
What you write, the files you attach, and what each task did (the sites it went to and its result) are read for things worth keeping. Page text itself is not stored.
Text you add here is not stored as it is: the Planner model picks the lasting facts out of it.
Passwords, keys and card numbers are never stored. To sign in, the agent relies on the passwords saved in your browser.
When memory is full, a new memory replaces the least useful one. With Fast mode on, Jev makes that choice.
Memories are stored on this device and sent to your model providers with each task.
